name: NFL Live Field
author: ant456
description: An arcade-style NFL show with three modes: live games (animated field, player cards with ESPN headshots and rarity frames, touchdown bursts with confetti), recently finished games (final score plus the same stat cards), and upcoming games (matchup and kickoff time). Pick favorite teams and switch on the favorites lock to show only their games in every mode. ESPN's public scoreboard, no API key.

versions.notes: The Govee helper now shares one listener, one lock and one activity log across all plugins (the core loads each plugin's modules in isolation, so each used to have its own), and every light trigger is logged, including why one was skipped.

New effect: rocket. It shoots up a sectioned light from the bottom to the top, bursts at the top and showers down like fireworks (on a light with no sections it swells, pops and sparkles out). A Reverse option per light handles lights mounted the other way up.

RGBIC support: effects now use a light's sections (a comet runs along it, fireworks pop on single sections, burst swaps alternating sections, glow fills up). Section counts are set in the Govee Lights portal. Home Assistant lights restore the scene they were playing.

Govee effects can now be set up in the Govee Lights portal: one shared settings file for every sports plugin, with per-sport overrides, re-read whenever it changes. The plugin's own govee block still works without the portal. Lights are restored reliably (verified and retried), and only one effect plays at a time across plugins.
Optional Govee light effects in the scoring team's colours (LAN or Home Assistant): burst, flash, pulse, chase, strobe, fireworks and glow, with the lights restored afterwards.

Fixed: drive arrows on the field were drawn mirrored (they marched the right way but pointed backwards). Stats: leaders are now also read from the competition-level list when ESPN does not put them on each team, routed to the right team by id, so player cards and the final-game stat ticker no longer come up empty in that case.

Fixed: the upcoming-game screen showed every kickoff as a bare date ('10/26 9:27 PM') because it was given the animation clock as 'now'. It now reads TODAY 9:27 PM, TMRW 1:00 PM, SUN 1:00 PM by calendar day (a game 13 hours away but tomorrow is TMRW, not a weekday).

Fixed: one failed player-photo download no longer aborts the rest of the batch (later players never loaded in test mode and live). Failures are now logged at warning level. Test mode with headshot_downloads on now fetches real ESPN photos instead of drawing synthetic faces. Fixed the demo id for Jalen Hurts.

Fixed: a real ESPN scoreboard fetch confirmed each team's stat leader is named 'passingLeader'/'rushingLeader'/'receivingLeader', not 'passingYards'/'rushingYards'/'receivingYards' as the parser expected -- so on real games, every team's leaders were silently dropped and no player cards or recap-panel stats ever had data to show. Both name forms are now accepted. The demo/test-mode data also now uses the real names, so this class of bug shows up in testing instead of only in production.

Recent (final) games no longer show the empty football field -- that space now holds an animated stat ticker of the game's top leaders: a staggered count-up per row and a spotlight that cycles between rows. Live games are unaffected (the field still shows there). Falls back to a plain message when a final game has no leaders data.

Adds recent (final-score) and upcoming (matchup preview) games as their own display modes, nfl_recent and nfl_upcoming, sharing the same ESPN scoreboard fetch as live -- no extra network calls. Recent games get the same player cards live games do. Selection uses the repo's usual other_*_games_to_show / other_rotation_interval_seconds / favorite_rotation_boost settings, and the favorites lock now applies to all three modes.

api_requirements.name: ESPN API
api_requirements.description: ESPN's public NFL scoreboard (scores, situation and per-team leaders) and ESPN player headshots. No API key.
